title: Error Handling
summary: Handle expected failures and keep real bugs visible.
refresher: JavaScript uses `throw` to report an error and `try/catch` to handle one. Catch errors when you know what to do next. Do not catch every error just to make the console quiet.

sections.title: Expected errors
sections.summary: Use try and catch for failures the program can handle.

blocks.body: Errors are not all the same. Some are expected, like bad user **input**. Some are bugs you need to fix. Good error handling tells those apart.
`try` holds the risky code. `catch` runs if that code throws. Keep the try block small so you can tell what failed.

blocks.caption: JSON.parse throws before the Loaded message, so catch provides a controlled response.

sections.title: Handle visible failures
sections.summary: Avoid empty catches and keep the failure cause clear.

blocks.caption: An empty catch makes the program look successful even though its work failed. Handle an expected case or preserve the error for a layer that can.

blocks.body: Trace the malformed **input**: parse begins, detects invalid syntax, creates a SyntaxError, and transfers control to catch. The original Error still matters during development, even when the message shown to a student is simpler.

blocks.title: Catch narrowly
blocks.body: Do not wrap a whole application in one broad try block. Keep the protected section close to the operation whose failure you understand, so unrelated programming mistakes are not mislabeled as expected **input** problems.

sections.title: Control-flow checks
sections.summary: Know when finally runs and why empty catch blocks are risky.

blocks.prompt: Which block runs whether try succeeds or fails?
blocks.why: A finally block runs after the try and any matching catch, making it suitable for cleanup that both paths require.

blocks.prompt: What is wrong with an empty catch block?
choices: It hides the failure and its evidence
It converts the error to text
blocks.why: The program silently continues, so neither the user nor the developer can see that save failed or why it failed.

blocks.title: Error Handling checklist
items: Use throw when code cannot safely continue.
Catch errors where you can recover.
Do not hide bugs by catching everything silently.

blocks.title: Common JavaScript error types
items: `SyntaxError`: JavaScript cannot parse the code or JSON text.
`TypeError`: code uses a value in a way that does not fit its type.
`ReferenceError`: code uses a name that is not defined.
`RangeError`: a number is outside the allowed range.
`URIError`: URI encoding or decoding receives invalid text.
